title: Ad Click Aggregation and Stream Analytics

nodes.label: User
nodes.summary: Sees an ad and clicks it; the click carries the id of the query or impression.

nodes.label: Advertiser
nodes.summary: Watches dashboards and is billed for valid clicks.

nodes.label: Ad serving
nodes.summary: Serves ads and logs the query or impression events that clicks later reference.

nodes.label: Click collector
nodes.summary: Receives clicks, assigns a unique click id, validates and writes to the replayable log. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Click log
nodes.summary: Partitioned, replayable log of raw clicks (kept so recovery can replay). Kafka-style systems let consumers rewind, which Flink's recovery needs.

nodes.label: Query / impression log
nodes.summary: Events logged by the ad server; a click references its query id.

nodes.label: Dedup and join
nodes.summary: Joins each click with its query and guarantees no duplicates in the output (at-most-once), with near-exact real-time results and exactly-once eventually. Runs independently in at least two datacenters.

nodes.label: Dispatcher
nodes.summary: Reads clicks, skips ids already in the registry, sends the rest to a joiner and retries with backoff (at-least-once input).

nodes.label: Joiner
nodes.summary: Stateless server that looks up the query, registers the click id with a retry token, then writes the joined click to the output log.

nodes.label: IdRegistry
nodes.summary: Replicated store of ids already joined in the last N days (3 in the paper's deployment); built on a Paxos-based key-value store with replicas in different regions, with server-side batching and sharding.

nodes.label: EventStore
nodes.summary: Looks up a query by id: an in-memory cache of recent queries backed by a log-based lookup.

nodes.label: Joined clicks log
nodes.summary: Deduplicated, enriched clicks used for billing and metrics.

nodes.label: Stream aggregator
nodes.summary: Counts clicks per ad per event-time window with a watermark, and checkpoints state with source offsets. Flink and Dataflow describe these mechanisms; the ad-specific job is our design.

nodes.label: Event-time windows
nodes.summary: Groups clicks by the time they happened rather than arrived; re-emits a window when late data arrives within the allowed lateness.

nodes.label: Watermark and late data
nodes.summary: A Watermark(t) declares that no more elements with timestamp up to t should arrive; most watermarks are heuristic, so later data is late and needs a policy.

nodes.label: Checkpoints
nodes.summary: Snapshots of operator state together with source positions, taken with barriers that flow in the stream; restart restores state and replays from the saved positions.

nodes.label: Aggregate store
nodes.summary: Stores totals by ad and window. Mesa (Google's ads aggregate store) uses versioned, strictly ordered batch updates with associative aggregation and negative facts for corrections; our reference design writes upserts by (ad, window) so re-emitted windows replace rather than add. Either way, applying the same input twice must not double count.

nodes.label: Batch reconciliation
nodes.summary: Recomputes totals from the raw log, compares them with the stream results and corrects them before billing. Photon likewise runs a verification system that finds clicks present in the registry but missing from the output.

nodes.label: Alternative: stream-only (Kappa-style) pipeline
nodes.summary: Rely on the replayable log and the stream engine alone, reprocessing the log for corrections instead of keeping a separate batch implementation. Trade-off depends on trust in replay and on logic differences.

steps.caption: The click arrives at the collector, which assigns a unique click id.
It is appended to the replayable click log.
The dispatcher reads it.
It checks the registry; an unseen id continues.
The click goes to a joiner.
The joiner finds the query the click refers to.
It registers the click id (with a retry token); only one joiner can succeed for an id.
The joined click is appended to the output log.
The aggregator counts it in the event-time window of the click.
The window total is upserted into the aggregate store.

flows.name: The same click is seen twice (failure mode)

steps.caption: A retry, or the pipeline in the second datacenter, reads the same click.
The registry already holds the id, so the dispatcher skips it; if a joiner races, only one registration succeeds and the other drops the event as a wasted join.

flows.name: A joiner crashes after registering the id (failure)

steps.caption: The id is registered but the joiner dies before writing output; no other joiner can write it.
The click is missing from the joined log.
Verification compares inputs with outputs; for a click missing from the output whose joiner crashed, it deletes the id and re-injects the event.

flows.name: A late click arrives after the watermark (failure mode)

steps.caption: A click arrives for a window that the watermark has passed.
Within the allowed lateness the window is re-emitted with the corrected count; beyond it the event goes to a late stream (our design reasoning).
Batch reconciliation folds the late clicks into the final totals.
The latest checkpoint holds operator state and the positions in the sources.
After restart the job restores the state and its sources (the joined clicks log) replay from the saved positions, so no click is lost or double counted in state.
Re-emitted windows overwrite the stored totals (upsert), so replayed output does not add twice.
The dispatcher in the failed datacenter stalls; the pipeline in the other datacenter keeps reading the same clicks.

Both pipelines share the IdRegistry, so the surviving one joins each click once. When the failed datacenter recovers, its dispatcher works through the backlog and skips clicks whose ids are already registered.
